title: Study: Asteroid Hit Created Two ‘Grand Canyons’ on Moon
speaker: VOA Learning English

sentences.en: A new study suggests an asteroid strike on the moon billions of years ago left two huge valleys about the size of Earth’s Grand Canyon.
sentences.zh: 一项新的研究表明,数十亿年前小行星对月球的撞击,留下了两个与地球大峡谷大小相近的巨大山谷。

sentences.en: Researchers from the United States and Britain said their research shows the two steep valleys, or canyons, likely formed in less than 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 美国和英国的研究人员说,他们的研究显示,两个陡峭的峡谷或峡谷可能在不到10分钟内形成。

sentences.en: They noted the crash, or impact, happened near the south pole on the far side of the moon.
sentences.zh: 他们注意到坠机或撞击发生在月球远方的南极附近。

sentences.en: That is the side of the moon which always faces away from Earth.
sentences.zh: 这是月球的一面 总是面对地球。

sentences.en: The area is known as the Schrödinger impact basin.
sentences.zh: 该地区被称为Schrödinger撞击盆地。

sentences.en: The speed of the incoming object – which the team said might have been a comet – was estimated to be around 55,000 kilometers per hour.
sentences.zh: 摄制组说,该物体可能是彗星,其速度估计约为每小时55 000公里。

sentences.en: The strike likely happened about 3.8 billion years ago.
sentences.zh: 罢工很可能发生在38亿年前。

sentences.en: The researchers used data collected by a spacecraft operated by the American space agency NASA.
sentences.zh: 研究人员使用了美国航天局运营的航天器收集的数据。

sentences.en: That vehicle, the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter , has been capturing lunar data since entering orbit around the moon in June 2009.
sentences.zh: 该飞行器,月球侦察轨道飞行器,自2009年6月进入环月轨道以来,一直在捕捉月球数据。

sentences.en: One main goal of the orbiter’s mission was to create a highly detailed, three-dimensional , or 3D, map of the moon.
sentences.zh: 该轨道器任务的一个主要目标是绘制一个非常详细、三维或三维的卫星地图。

sentences.en: The data has been used by NASA to learn more about lunar resources and to plan for future missions.
sentences.zh: 美国航天局利用这些数据更多地了解月球资源,并为今后的飞行任务进行规划。

sentences.en: The agency noted that the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter had “already collected as much data as all other planetary missions combined.”
sentences.zh: 该机构指出,月球侦察轨道器“已经收集了与所有其他行星飞行任务合计的数据一样多的数据”。

sentences.en: The team studying the canyons used the orbiter’s map data to simulate the path of the incoming object, as well as material that was displaced by the crash.
sentences.zh: 研究峡谷的小组利用轨道器的地图数据模拟进入物体的路径以及坠毁时被移位的材料。

sentences.en: The scientists recently published a study describing their results in Nature Communications .
sentences.zh: 科学家们最近发表了一项研究报告,

sentences.en: The group’s simulations suggested the space rock passed over the south pole before hitting.
sentences.zh: 该组的模拟表明,该空间岩石在撞击之前越过了南极。

sentences.en: It then created a huge basin and launched rocky materials at speeds up to 1 kilometer per second.
sentences.zh: 然后,它创造了一个巨大的盆地,以每秒1公里的速度发射了岩石材料。

sentences.en: The researchers said material was sent flying and struck the lunar surface like missiles.
sentences.zh: 研究人员说,材料被送去飞行,像导弹一样击中月球表面。

sentences.en: This resulted in the creation of the canyons.
sentences.zh: 这导致了峡谷的建立。

sentences.en: The team said the canyons appear comparable in size to the Grand Canyon, in the U.S. state of Arizona.
sentences.zh: 队伍说峡谷的大小 与美国亚利桑那州的大峡谷相似

sentences.en: The study’s lead writer was David Kring of the Lunar and Planetary Institute in Houston.
sentences.zh: 研究的主要作者是休斯顿月球和行星研究所的David Kring。

sentences.en: He told the Associated Press that findings suggest the asteroid strike was a “very violent” geologic process.
sentences.zh: 他告诉美联社,发现小行星撞击是一个“非常猛烈”的地质过程。

sentences.en: Kring and his team estimated the asteroid was 25 kilometers across.
sentences.zh: 克林和他的团队估计这颗小行星相隔25公里

sentences.en: They estimated that the energy needed to create the two canyons would have been more than 130 times greater than the power of all the world’s current nuclear weapons.
sentences.zh: 他们估计,建立这两座峡谷所需的能量会比世界目前所有核武器的能量大130倍以上。

sentences.en: Kring said most of the rock and debris was thrown in a direction away from the south pole.
sentences.zh: 克林说大部分的岩石和碎片 被扔向远离南极的一个方向

sentences.en: That finding is good news for NASA which plans to land astronauts in that area in the future.
sentences.zh: 这一发现是美国航天局的好消息,美国航天局计划今后在该地区降落宇航员。

sentences.en: Kring noted it should improve the exploration possibilities of future astronauts.
sentences.zh: Kring指出,它应当改进未来宇航员的探索可能性。

sentences.en: "Because debris from the Schrödinger impact was jettisoned away from the lunar south pole, ancient rocks in the polar region will be at or close to the surface…,” Kring told Reuters news agency.
sentences.zh: "因为施罗丁格撞击的碎片 被抛离了月球南极, 极地的古老岩石 将位于或接近表面..." Kring告诉路透社。

sentences.en: This should make it easier for future American astronauts to collect them.
sentences.zh: 这将使未来的美国宇航员更容易收集。

sentences.en: NASA’s future lunar exploration plans are known as the agency’s Artemis program.
sentences.zh: 美国航天局未来的月球探索计划被称为该机构的Artemis计划。

sentences.en: The program aims to return astronauts to the moon for the first time since NASA’s Apollo 17 mission in 1972.
sentences.zh: 该方案旨在使航天员返回月球,这是美国航天局1972年阿波罗17号飞行任务以来的第一次。

sentences.en: The agency’s current plan is to send astronauts on a trip around the moon next year.
sentences.zh: 该公司目前的计划是明年派遣宇航员环绕月球旅行。

sentences.en: That would be followed a year or so later by a landing attempt on the lunar surface.
sentences.zh: 之后一年左右 月球表面的着陆尝试

sentences.en: The researchers said older rocks in the area can help scientists gain a better understanding of the moon’s past history.
sentences.zh: 研究人员说,该地区老化的岩石可以帮助科学家更好地了解月球的历史。

sentences.en: They could also help answer questions about the formation of Earth.
sentences.zh: 他们还可以帮助回答关于地球形成的问题。

sentences.en: Kring noted it is currently not clear whether the two huge canyons are permanently shadowed like some of the craters at the moon’s south pole. “That is something that we’re clearly going to be reexamining,” he said.
sentences.zh: 克林指出,目前尚不清楚这两座巨大的峡谷是否像月球南极的一些弹坑一样被永久地蒙上阴影。 他说 : “ 我们显然要重新审查这一点。 ”

sentences.en: I’m Bryan Lynn. Bryan Lynn wrote this story for VOA Learning English, based on reports from The Associated Press, Reuters, The Universities Space Research Association and Nature Communications.
sentences.zh: 我是布莱恩·林恩。布莱恩·林恩根据美联社、路透社、大学空间研究协会和自然通讯社的报告,为VOA学习英语撰写了这个故事。
